title: Postgres: i32/INTEGER used for BOOLEAN columns
description:
Multiple functions use i32 types for columns that are BOOLEAN in postgres. PostgreSQL does not implicitly cast between INTEGER and BOOLEAN in either direction, so both reads AND writes will fail at runtime on postgres.

WRITE path issues (binding i32 to BOOLEAN):

articles_db.rs:
1. create_article (lines 243-261): binds rtl_int, pinned_int, draft_int as i32 to BOOLEAN columns
2. update_article (lines 394-409): binds rtl as Option<i32> to BOOLEAN column
3. pin_article (line 470): SQL literal 'pinned = 1' -- should be TRUE
4. unpin_article (line 486): SQL literal 'pinned = 0' -- should be FALSE
5. list_collection_articles (line 337): SQL literal 'draft = 0' -- should be FALSE

books_db.rs:
6. create_review (line 463): binds spoiler_int as i32 to BOOLEAN column

READ path issues (decoding BOOLEAN into i32 tuple):

books_db.rs:
7. ReviewTuple (line 438): position 7 is i32, but postgres spoiler column is BOOLEAN. sqlx::query_as will fail decoding BOOLEAN into i32.

The sqlite paths work correctly because sqlite stores booleans as INTEGER. All tests use sqlite, so these bugs are not caught by tests.

Fix: use TRUE/FALSE SQL literals in postgres queries, bind bool values in postgres arms, and use bool in tuple types (or split tuple types per-backend).

Files:
- /home/mark/PROJECT/fedistract/fieldwork-db/src/articles_db.rs
- /home/mark/PROJECT/fedistract/fieldwork-db/src/books_db.rs
close_reason: Fixed: Postgres branches now bind native bool. SQLite branches keep i32 conversion. pin/unpin use true/false in Postgres SQL.
